documents.title: 社交媒体与面对面交流
documents.taskPrompt: Social media is replacing face-to-face communication for many people. Is this a positive or negative development?
documents.essay:
Social media is now a normal part of daily communication. It helps people stay connected across distance, but I believe replacing too much face-to-face contact is mostly a negative development.

The main advantage is convenience. Students who study abroad can speak with their families without paying high phone costs. Friends can also share news quickly, and shy people may find it easier to start a conversation online. These benefits are important, especially when people cannot meet because they live far apart.

However, online messages do not always show feelings clearly. A short reply may look rude even when the writer is only busy. More importantly, people may have hundreds of online contacts but nobody nearby when they need practical help. Face-to-face meetings allow people to notice tone, body language and changes in another person's mood. This is especially valuable during serious conversations about health, family problems or conflict.

The best solution is not to reject social media. People can use it to arrange meetings and maintain relationships between visits. Schools and workplaces can also create activities where phones are not needed. For example, a team can discuss a difficult problem in person and use a group chat later for simple updates. In this way, each form of communication is used for the task it handles well.

This balance matters because convenient contact is not always meaningful contact.

In conclusion, social media is useful for keeping contact, but it should support rather than replace direct communication. Sensitive or complicated needs still require real human presence.

documents.title: 城市公交免费
documents.taskPrompt: Some people think public transport should be free for everyone. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
documents.essay:
Public transport is essential in large cities, and some people argue that everyone should use it without paying. I agree that fares should be low, but I do not think a completely free system is always the best use of public money.

Free buses and trains could encourage some drivers to leave their cars at home. This may reduce traffic and air pollution. It would also help people with low incomes travel to work, school and medical appointments. These are strong reasons for governments to support public transport with taxes.

Nevertheless, making every journey free can be very expensive. Wealthy commuters who can easily pay would receive the same support as people who struggle with basic costs. If the transport budget is limited, money spent removing all fares may leave less for more frequent buses, safer stations and routes in outer areas. A free service that is crowded and unreliable will not persuade many car users to change.

A better policy is to keep fares affordable and offer free or cheaper travel to children, older people and low-income workers. Cities should also improve service before expecting people to stop driving. This approach directs more help to passengers who need it while keeping enough money for maintenance. The exact balance will differ between cities because their tax income and transport networks are not the same.

This choice also keeps public support clear.

In conclusion, public transport deserves strong public funding, but universal free travel is not automatically fair or effective. Targeted support and better service may produce greater benefits.

documents.title: 高中毕业间隔年
documents.taskPrompt: Some students take a year off after finishing school before starting university. Do the advantages outweigh the disadvantages?
documents.essay:
Taking a year off before university is becoming common in some countries. I think it can be helpful, although its value depends on whether a student has a clear and realistic plan.

During a gap year, young people may work, travel or volunteer. A job can teach them to arrive on time, deal with customers and manage money. Travel can make them more independent because they must solve ordinary problems away from home. Students may also have time to think carefully about their subject instead of choosing a degree only because their friends chose it.

There are also risks. A long break can make academic routines harder to restart. Travel and unpaid volunteering may be possible mainly for families with more money, so the experience is not equally available. Some students also describe a gap year as useful when they actually spend most of it without a goal. In that case, they lose time but gain little experience.

For these reasons, schools should not present a gap year as the correct choice for everyone. They can help interested students make a simple plan with a budget, a main activity and a date for applying to university. Students who already know what they want to study may prefer to continue directly. Others who are uncertain could benefit from several months of work or community activity.

In conclusion, a gap year has more advantages when it includes purposeful activity and remains affordable. Without these conditions, going straight to university may be the safer option.

documents.title: 本地食品与进口食品
documents.taskPrompt: Countries should try to produce all the food their population needs and import as little as possible. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
documents.essay:
Some people believe countries should grow almost all of their own food. I agree that local production is important, but depending only on domestic farms would create new risks.

Local food can travel a shorter distance, which may reduce transport pollution and keep money in rural communities. Farmers also understand local soil and weather. During an international crisis, domestic production can prevent a country from becoming too dependent on distant suppliers. Governments therefore have good reasons to protect basic farming skills and land.

However, no country can efficiently produce every kind of food. Climate, water and available land are different. Growing unsuitable crops may require heated buildings or large amounts of water, causing more environmental damage than importing them. A poor harvest caused by drought or disease would also be more dangerous if there were no outside suppliers.

The safer approach is to avoid relying on a single source. Countries can produce important basic foods at home while trading for products that other regions grow more efficiently. They can also keep several import partners instead of buying everything from one country. Clear information about environmental standards can help consumers choose responsibly. This mixed system supports local farmers but still gives shoppers variety and protects the food supply when one region has a bad season.

It also prevents one policy goal from creating another weakness.

In conclusion, countries should strengthen local farming, but minimum imports are not a sensible goal by themselves. A balance of domestic production and varied trade is more practical and resilient.

documents.title: 机器人照顾老年人
documents.taskPrompt: Robots are increasingly used to care for older people. Is this a positive or negative development?
documents.essay:
Robots are beginning to help older people at home and in care centres. I believe this is a positive development when robots support human carers, but it becomes negative if they replace personal contact.

Robots can perform useful routine tasks. They can remind a person to take medicine, carry heavy objects and call for help after a fall. This support may allow some older people to live independently for longer. It can also reduce physical pressure on care workers, who often have many patients and limited time.

However, care is not only a list of tasks. An older person may feel lonely, worried or confused, and a machine cannot fully understand these feelings. Even a polite voice from a robot is not the same as a conversation with somebody who remembers the person's life. There are also safety concerns if the technology fails or private health information is collected without clear permission.

Care providers should therefore use robots for repeated and physical work while keeping people responsible for emotional support and important decisions. Families and staff must be able to check what the machine records. Older users should also have the right to refuse a device that makes them uncomfortable. Technology is most useful when it gives carers more time to speak with residents instead of being used mainly to reduce staff numbers.

Regular human visits should remain guaranteed.

In conclusion, robots can improve safety and independence, but they should remain an extra tool. Human presence is still necessary for trust, comfort and complex needs.

documents.title: 博物馆免费开放
documents.taskPrompt: Some people think museums should be free, while others believe visitors should pay an entrance fee. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
documents.essay:
Museums preserve history and culture, so there is debate about whether visitors should pay. In my view, basic access should be free or very cheap, while special exhibitions can charge a reasonable fee.

Free entry allows more people to learn from museums. Families with limited incomes may visit more often, and students can use collections for school projects. Museums supported by public taxes also belong partly to the public, so another high charge can seem unfair. More visitors may also spend money in nearby cafes and shops.

On the other hand, museums need money to protect objects, pay staff and improve displays. Government funding can change from year to year, and donations are uncertain. Entrance fees provide a direct source of income. They may also reduce overcrowding at very popular sites, where too many visitors can damage the experience and even the collection.

A mixed system can meet both needs. Permanent collections could be free on most days, with paid temporary exhibitions and optional membership. Governments can give extra support to smaller museums that serve local communities. Popular institutions may use timed tickets instead of high prices to control numbers. This keeps the public door open without pretending that buildings and conservation have no cost. It also targets free access at the central educational service rather than giving every additional activity away.

This balance can make funding decisions easier to explain to the public.

In conclusion, museums should remove major price barriers to their main collections, but charging for some services is reasonable when the income clearly supports their work.

documents.title: 学校教授理财
documents.taskPrompt: Schools should teach children how to manage money. Do you agree or disagree?
documents.essay:
Many young adults leave school without knowing how to plan their spending. I agree that schools should teach basic money management, although it should be a small practical part of education rather than a large new subject.

Students will soon need to understand wages, bills, bank accounts and borrowing. Without simple knowledge, they may accept an expensive loan or spend all their income before necessary costs are paid. Not every family can explain these topics, and advice at home may depend on the parents' own experience. School can provide a common starting point for all children.

Lessons should focus on realistic decisions instead of difficult financial theory. Students could compare two phone contracts, plan a weekly food budget or calculate the total cost of borrowing. These tasks connect mathematics with daily life. They should also discuss advertising and online scams, because young people increasingly make payments through phones.

However, schools already have busy timetables. Money lessons should not remove essential reading, science or mathematics classes. A short unit each year could be included in mathematics or citizenship education. Teachers also need neutral materials so that lessons do not become advertisements for a particular bank. The aim is not to tell children how to become rich, but to help them recognise costs, risks and basic choices.

It also gives teachers a clear and limited responsibility.

In conclusion, practical financial education should be available to every student. A limited, useful programme can prepare them for adult responsibilities without crowding out core academic learning.

documents.title: 四天工作制
documents.taskPrompt: A four-day working week should replace the traditional five-day week. Do you agree or disagree?
documents.essay:
A four-day working week has attracted attention because many employees want a better balance between work and life. I partly agree with this change, but it cannot suit every job in the same form.

An extra free day may reduce stress and give workers more time for family, exercise or rest. Some employees could become more focused because they are less tired. Companies may also find it easier to keep skilled staff. If the same work is completed in fewer hours, both workers and employers can benefit.

However, shorter weeks can create pressure when the workload does not change. Employees may need to work very long days or answer messages on their day off. Hospitals, shops and transport services must operate throughout the week, so they cannot simply close for three days. Hiring more staff would increase costs, especially for small businesses.

For this reason, companies should test the policy instead of treating it as a universal rule. Office teams may reduce unnecessary meetings and measure completed work during a trial. Services that need continuous cover could use different shifts rather than giving everyone the same day off. Managers should check whether stress, customer waiting time and unfinished work improve or become worse. A trial can be stopped or adjusted if the result is poor.

Workers should help judge the trial because managers may miss hidden pressure.

In conclusion, a four-day week can be positive in suitable workplaces, but flexibility is more sensible than a national replacement of every five-day schedule.

documents.title: 新闻过度报道负面事件
documents.taskPrompt: News reports focus too much on problems and emergencies rather than positive developments. Why is this, and is it a negative trend?
documents.essay:
News programmes often give more space to crime, disasters and political conflict than to positive changes. This happens for understandable reasons, but I think the overall trend is harmful when it gives people an unbalanced picture of society.

Negative events are usually sudden and easy to present as a clear story. A fire or election argument has immediate images, while a gradual improvement in public health may take years and needs more explanation. News companies also compete for attention. Frightening headlines can make people click quickly, so editors may choose them even when the event has little effect on most readers.

Reporting serious problems is necessary. People need warnings about dangerous weather, dishonest officials or unsafe products. Such reporting can push authorities to act. The problem begins when repeated negative stories make rare dangers seem normal. Viewers may believe their neighbourhood is becoming unsafe even when local crime is falling. Constant bad news can also make people feel that action is useless.

Editors should not create cheerful stories simply to make audiences comfortable. Instead, reports about problems can include context, such as whether the situation is improving and what responses have worked elsewhere. News organisations can also cover slow positive changes when they are supported by evidence. This would not hide real emergencies, but it would help audiences judge their size more accurately.

In conclusion, negative news attracts attention and often concerns urgent events, but excessive focus can distort risk and reduce public confidence. More context would make reporting more useful.

documents.title: 维修还是更换产品
documents.taskPrompt: Many people replace broken products instead of repairing them. Why is this happening, and what problems can it cause?
documents.essay:
Many household products are thrown away soon after they break. People often replace them because buying a new item is easier, but this habit creates environmental and financial problems.

Modern products can be difficult to repair. Some phones and appliances are sealed, and spare parts are expensive or unavailable. Repair shops may charge almost as much as a new product because skilled work takes time. Advertising also presents newer models as faster and more attractive, so consumers may feel that an old item is no longer worth keeping.

The main result is more waste. Electronic products contain plastic, metal and chemicals, and safe recycling is not always available. Producing replacements also uses energy and raw materials. At the household level, frequent small purchases can become a large cost. The cheapest product may save money today but cost more if it breaks every year.

Governments can require manufacturers to provide spare parts and repair information for a reasonable period. Products could carry a simple label showing how easily they can be repaired. Consumers would then compare expected lifetime, not only the price in the shop. Repair services also need clear prices, because people will not choose them if the final cost is uncertain. These steps cannot make every old product worth fixing, especially when it is unsafe or uses too much energy, but they can make repair a realistic option.

In conclusion, replacement is often convenient because products and prices are designed that way. Better information and access to repair could reduce waste without forcing people to keep unsafe goods.
